value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for proving a code project's capabilities are wired in
value.lets_workers: Prove that what a code project has written and tested is actually reachable: find modules no live path imports, check that every config field survives a save and reload, check that every health probe fails when its dependency stops, give every rule a canary its check must catch, and confirm each documented behavior has a test that runs the real path rather than a mock. Every gap becomes a finding in the findings to fixes pack's shape. Tested standard-library code finds unused modules, mock-only tests and hollow probes in Python packages.
value.not_for: Deciding what the code should do, or reviewing its security; the repository review and security review packs do those.

flow.when: Entry points, config schemas, probes, docs and rules, at one commit.
The import graph from the entry points, then a runtime trace.
Every config field saved, reloaded and compared.
Hollow probes found statically, the rest run with dependencies stopped.
Each documented behavior, its real path and its tests' patches.
One known-bad canary per rule, caught by its check.
One finding per gap, in the findings to fixes shape.
Every rule's result, canary and finding in one report.
Each finding triaged, then a fix proposed and verified.

value.worked_example: Synthetic: a food pantry's appointment app. The module map finds two dark modules, one only tests reach, one used only for type checking and two that a computed import name could load, which a runtime trace confirms. One setting is lost on reload and unknown keys vanish. Three probes are hollow on their face, and a fourth passes with its database stopped. Two documented behaviors are covered only by tests that patch their own path, and one has no test. Twelve findings follow.

value.title: How wiring and conformance are checked, from scope to findings
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: scope-wiring names the commit, packages, entry points, config schemas, probes, docs and rules.
find-unused-modules, check-config-round-trip, check-health-probes and map-behaviors-to-tests each run one rule in a local copy and record what they saw.
plant-canaries gives every rule a known-bad example its check must catch.
record-wiring-findings writes one finding per gap; compile-conformance-report puts every rule's result, canary and finding in one report.
The findings to fixes pack triages, fixes and verifies each finding; the report is compiled again at the fixed commit.
rules: Static reading finds leads and a check that ran decides: confirm a dark module with a runtime import trace from every entry point, and a probe with its dependency stopped.
Work in a local copy at the exact commit; nothing outside that copy is read or changed.
A check never deletes or rewires anything. A gap becomes a finding whose fix proposal says wire it in or remove it, and a person decides.
Mocks at the edges, such as the clock, the network or a payment provider, are fine; a mock on the documented path is not coverage.
Canaries live in the test tree, never on a live path.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

value.title: What a live path is, and how modules are classified
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same source and entry points give the same map.
entry_points: Console and GUI scripts and plugin entry points declared in packaging metadata.
Server, worker and scheduled-job start-up modules a deployment runs.
Modules a deployment loads by configuration, such as a plugin list in a settings file, named in the scope.
counts_as_an_import: import x and from x import y, absolute or relative.
Importing a submodule, which loads its parent packages.
importlib.import_module or __import__ with a constant name.
An import inside a function, which runs when the function does.
does_not_count: An import only under if TYPE_CHECKING.
An import from a module that is itself dark.

statuses.live: Reached from an entry point through imports that run.
statuses.dynamic_candidate: Could be loaded by a computed import name; a runtime trace settles it.
statuses.type_only: Reached only for type checking; not a gap.
statuses.test_only: Reached only from tests; a gap.

rules: A computed module name leaves the graph open: list the call, and settle the modules its prefix could load with a trace.
Before recording a dark or test-only module, run every entry point in a local copy with python -X importtime, or a dump of sys.modules, and confirm it never loads.

value.title: Config fields survive a save and a reload
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same schema and values give the same results.
rules: For every field in the config schema, set a value that differs from its default, save it with the project's own writer, load it with its own reader and compare.
Load, save and load again: the second load equals the first. Stability alone does not prove a field survives; a lost field is stable at its default.
A field read back as its default, or missing, is lost; one read back as another value is changed.
A field the code never reads after loading is not_read: it is wired to nothing.
An unknown key is rejected with an error or preserved; dropping it silently is a gap.
Round-trip environment and command-line overrides separately.
Use synthetic values only; never put a real secret in a fixture.

value.title: A health probe probes
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same probe and stopped dependency give the same result.
rules: A probe probes a dependency when stopping that dependency makes it fail or report degraded within its timeout, and restoring it makes it healthy again.
Stop each dependency the probe claims to cover, in a local copy only: a database, a queue, a cache, an upstream service, a disk or a model endpoint.
A probe that returns a constant, or only a flag set at start-up, is hollow whatever its tests say.
A probe that calls a dependency but ignores the answer is hollow too; only the stopped run shows it.
Liveness checks the process itself and does not fail because a downstream dependency is down; readiness checks the dependencies traffic needs.
A probe answers within its caller's timeout and changes nothing it checks.

static_kinds.flag_only: Reads a remembered state; probes no dependency.
static_kinds.calls: Calls something; a lead until the stopped run.

value.title: Each documented behavior has a test of its real path
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same map and tests give the same statuses.
rules: List each behavior the docs, help text or API description promise as one sentence, with where it is promised.
Name its real path: the dotted names from the entry people reach to the effect.
Map each behavior to the tests said to cover it, and record what every test patches.
real_path: at least one listed test patches nothing on the path. mock_only: every listed test does. untested: no listed test exists.
A behavior that needs an outside service gets a contract test against a recorded exchange, not a mock of its own path.
A test that patches nothing may still not reach the entry; read it to confirm that it does.

value.purpose: Checks every conformance report must pass before anyone relies on it. The two synthetic good reports, one with gaps and their findings and one after the fixes, pass all of them; each synthetic bad report fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: A conformance report is about one exact commit.
Live paths start from named entry points, each with the reason it runs.
The four rules all ran: modules, config round trips, probes and behaviors.
A rule that did not run makes the report incomplete.
Every rule names its command and its evidence.
Every rule has a canary, and the run that caught it.
Every gap is a finding in the findings to fixes shape.
A behavior counted as covered names where it is promised and the tests that run it.
A behavior counted as covered has no test patching its real path.
A verified probe failed when its dependency stopped.
A verified probe recovered when its dependency came back.
Every report says what it does not show.

value.title: Tool card: the wiring checks
value.category_reason: Tested code a worker runs inside a claimed verb, pinned by path, file count and digest.
value.name: wiring checks
value.runtime: Python 3.10 or later, standard library only; nothing to install.
commands: python -m wiring_checks modules ROOT [--package NAME] [--entry MODULE] [--tests PATH] [--pyproject FILE] [--base DIR] [--strict]
python -m wiring_checks mocks PATH [PATH ...] [--behaviors FILE] [--base DIR]
python -m wiring_checks probes ROOT [PATH ...] [--names REGEX] [--base DIR]
does: Classifies every module of a Python package as live, dynamic_candidate, type_only, test_only or dark from its import graph and entry points.
Lists what every test patches through unittest.mock or monkeypatch, and marks each documented behavior real_path, mock_only or untested.
Finds health probes by name or route and marks each constant, flag_only or calls.
does_not: Import or run the code it reads, start a dependency or call a probe.
Open a network connection, call a model or write any file.
Decide anything: static results are leads for the verbs' runtime checks.
value.tests: The code's tests cover every rule on small synthetic packages and on a synthetic pantry app, and recompute this pack's module map, behavior map and probe scan from source.json, in the library's CI job for the pack.
